# Results — Study 347 (Look-Ahead-Bias) on a real tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One ordinary signal — a
20-day causal z-score **momentum** rule — run on the *same* daily SPY tape under two
execution conventions: **peek** (same-bar fill: the position formed at the close of `t`
earns the return *of* `t`, the bar that produced the signal — the look-ahead bug) and
**lag1** (the desk's one-execution-lag rule: signal at the close of `t` earns the return
of `t+1`). As-of **2026-05-29** (the last full month — the in-progress June bar is
dropped); match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tape | `SPY` daily total-return adjusted closes (Yahoo! Finance) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (5,385 trading days) |
| Fingerprint | `b20030e8a296` |
| Signal | 20-day causal z-score momentum, position `+tanh(z_t)` ∈ (−1, 1) |

## The headline — the look-ahead tax (real SPY)

| Convention | Sharpe | HAC *t* | CAGR | What it is |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **peek** (same-bar fill, look-ahead) | **+4.87** | **+28.07** | +97.7% | a backtest fantasy |
| **lag1** (correct one-bar lag) | **−0.14** | −0.77 | −3.0% | the honest, untradable truth |

- **Sharpe inflation: +5.01.** A nothing strategy (the lagged momentum rule has *no*
  edge: HAC *t* = −0.77, indistinguishable from zero) becomes a Sharpe-4.9, *t* = 28
  monster the instant the position is allowed to earn the bar that created it.
- **The bias is not an edge, so costs don't touch it.** At 5 bps/side the peek Sharpe is
  still **+4.69** (*t* = 27.0) while the honest lag drifts to −0.33. Look-ahead manufactures
  *contemporaneous correlation*, which transaction costs cannot erode — that is exactly why
  a look-ahead backtest looks "robust."
- **The mechanism, named.** `+tanh(z_t)` is large and positive precisely on the days the
  price just rose; letting that position earn *the same day's* return is mechanically
  ~`pos · ret` with `pos` built from `ret`. The "alpha" is the signal correlating with the
  data that defined it — a tautology, not a forecast.

## Synthetic controls — the harness is honest

A deterministic offline panel (`data.synthetic_prices`) plants a *fairly tradable*
mean-reversion edge (the pull on day `t+1` depends only on the z-score known at the close
of `t`), and a pure random walk for the null. The **reversion** signal is run lagged:

| Tape | lag1 Sharpe (*t*) | peek Sharpe (*t*) | Reading |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| null (edge = 0, random walk) | −0.03 (−0.11) | −6.36 (−27.73) | lag1 ≈ 0 (no edge to find — clean **negative control**); peek still manufactures a huge biased Sharpe |
| edge = 0.002 (planted reversion) | +3.17 (+12.82) | −6.57 (−32.77) | lag1 banks the *real* edge (**positive control passes**); the peek has the *wrong sign* — it is contemporaneous correlation, not the signal |

The peek's sign **flips** between the momentum headline (positive) and the reversion
control (negative) while always being large and significant — the signature of a bias
locked to the contemporaneous return, not to any genuine forecast.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The *correctly lagged*, actually-tradable momentum rule has no edge
  on this tape (HAC *t* = −0.77). There is nothing real here; the headline is an artefact.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The Sharpe-4.9 "strategy" requires trading on the close that
  has not yet happened. It cannot be executed by anyone, at any cost — the definition of a
  mirage.
- **Does a one-bar peek inflate the backtest? — CONFIRMED.** Yes, enormously and
  cost-proof: a zero-edge rule becomes Sharpe ~4.9 (*t* = 28) on real SPY, and a planted
  positive control is only bankable with the correct one-bar lag. This is the empirical
  case for the desk's **one-execution-lag rule** — *signal known at the close of `t` earns
  the return of `t+1`, one `shift`, applied once.*
